post_topic: API integration failures that aren't code bugs — why direct endpoint verification catches what docs and assumptions miss
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top center in bold: "Verify at the Wire" with subtitle: "Two failures. Neither was your code."

Diagram layout: left to right flow with two parallel horizontal lanes, stacked vertically, each representing one API check scenario. A shared starting node on the far left labeled "curl" with a terminal icon anchors both lanes.

Top lane label: "Scenario A — Free Tier Key". Nodes left to right: box labeled "Valid API Key" → arrow labeled "HTTP Request" → box labeled "Live API Endpoint" → arrow labeled "403 Forbidden" in amber #F5A623 → red-outlined box labeled "Tier has no API access" with a lock icon. Below this final node, a small callout bubble in amber: "Not an auth bug. A tier bug."

Bottom lane label: "Scenario B — Valid Key, Missing Endpoint". Nodes left to right: box labeled "Valid API Key" → arrow labeled "HTTP Request" → box labeled "Live API Endpoint" → arrow labeled "404 Not Found" in amber #F5A623 → red-outlined box labeled "Endpoint not in production" with a broken-link icon. Below this final node, a small callout bubble in amber: "Docs say it exists. API doesn't."

Below both lanes, a wide horizontal box spanning the full width in navy #0A0F1E with white text: "Trust the live surface — not the documentation of the live surface."

All boxes and arrows use navy #0A0F1E strokes and labels. Failure nodes and arrows use amber #F5A623. Lane labels use blue #5a96ff. No logos needed for this diagram.

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
